questionText:
At 1 July 2025, Tariq Traders had net assets of **Rs. 1,450,000**. During the year ended 30 June 2026, the following transactions took place:

| Transaction Particulars | Amount (Rs.) |
| :--- | ---: |
| Additional capital introduced by owner | 320,000 |
| Cash drawings by owner | 140,000 |
| Goods taken by owner for personal use (Cost: Rs. 45,000; Selling price: Rs. 60,000) | 45,000 |
| Closing Net Assets at 30 June 2026 | 1,980,000 |

What is the net profit earned by Tariq Traders for the year ended 30 June 2026?
Which of the following accounting concepts requires that non-current assets be valued at historical cost less accumulated depreciation rather than forced liquidation value?

chapterName: Books of Prime Entry & Trial Balance
questionText:
A trial balance extracted by **Mehran Enterprises** at 31 December 2025 failed to agree, and a Suspense Account was opened. Subsequent investigation revealed:

| Error Ref | Error Description | Amount (Rs.) |
| :--- | :--- | ---: |
| 1 | Sales day book was overcast by | 18,500 |
| 2 | Discount allowed was credited to Discount Received account | 6,200 |
| 3 | Purchase of office furniture debited to Purchases account | 95,000 |

If the draft net profit before correcting these errors was **Rs. 640,000**, what is the revised net profit after correction (ignoring depreciation on furniture)?

chapterName: Books of Prime Entry & Trial Balance
questionText:
The following incomplete **Trade Receivables Control Account (T-Account)** has been prepared by a junior bookkeeper for the month of May 2026:

| Dr. Particulars | Amount (Rs.) | Cr. Particulars | Amount (Rs.) |
| :--- | ---: | :--- | ---: |
| Balance b/d (1 May 2026) | 480,000 | Cash & Bank receipts from credit customers | 1,120,000 |
| Credit Sales during May | 1,350,000 | Sales Returns Inwards | 42,000 |
| Dishonoured cheques from customers | 28,000 | Irrecoverable debts written off | 18,000 |
| | | Contra settlement with Payables Ledger | 35,000 |

What is the closing debit balance (**Balance c/d**) on the Trade Receivables Control Account at 31 May 2026?

The Cash Book (Bank column) of **Indus Associates** shows a credit balance (overdraft) of **Rs. 84,000** at 31 March 2026. The following differences were identified upon comparison with the Bank Statement:

| Item | Amount (Rs.) |
| :--- | ---: |
| Unpresented cheques at 31 March 2026 | 46,000 |
| Uncredited deposits in transit | 68,000 |
| Bank charges appearing only on Bank Statement | 3,500 |
| Direct credit by a customer into bank account | 29,500 |
| Dishonoured cheque from customer (not yet recorded in Cash Book) | 14,000 |

What is the **corrected Cash Book balance** at 31 March 2026?

Continuing from an adjusted Cash Book overdraft of **Rs. 72,000**, if unpresented cheques are **Rs. 46,000** and uncredited deposits are **Rs. 68,000**, what balance was shown on the Bank Statement at 31 March 2026?

At 1 January 2025, **Khyber Co.** had an Allowance for Doubtful Debts of **Rs. 75,000**. At 31 December 2025, gross trade receivables stood at **Rs. 1,680,000**. It was decided to:
1. Write off an irrecoverable balance of **Rs. 30,000**.
2. Make a specific allowance of **100%** against a bankrupt customer owing **Rs. 50,000**.
3. Maintain a general allowance of **4%** on the remaining trade receivables.

What is the net charge for Irrecoverable & Doubtful Debts Expense in the Statement of Profit or Loss for 2025?

A company pays insurance annually in advance on **1 October** each year. The annual premiums paid were:
- **1 October 2024:** Rs. 240,000
- **1 October 2025:** Rs. 300,000

For the financial year ended **31 December 2025**, what are the **Insurance Expense** in Profit or Loss and the **Prepaid Insurance** in the Statement of Financial Position?

chapterName: IAS 16 Property, Plant & Equipment and IAS 2 Inventories
questionText:
A manufacturing plant was acquired on **1 January 2023** for **Rs. 4,000,000** and depreciated at **20% per annum on the reducing balance method**. On **1 July 2025**, the plant was traded in for a new machine costing **Rs. 5,200,000**, with a trade-in allowance of **Rs. 2,100,000** agreed by the vendor. Depreciation is charged on a monthly pro-rata basis.

What is the gain or loss on disposal of the old plant on 1 July 2025?

questionText:
